newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pro-Taleban forces capture northern city of Kunduz.
newsitem.headline: Pro-Taleban forces capture northern city of Kunduz.

text.p: Pro-Taleban forces have captured the northern city of Kunduz, forcing a commander loyal to opposition leader Ahmad Shah Masood to flee, a Pakistan-based news agency reported on Wednesday.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said local commanders allied with the purist Islamic militia had gained control of the city, about 250 km (160 miles) north of Kabul, on Tuesday evening.

AIP said a mixed force of Taleban and fighters loyal to mainly ethnic Pashtun local commanders had forced one of Masood's commanders, Mir Alam, to flee to the border with Tajikistan, though it was not clear if he had crossed it.
The local commanders had previously shown sympathy for the Taleban, putting up white Taleban flags in their areas when the Taleban controlled the northern capital of Mazar-i-Sharif.

A Taleban force was driven from Mazar-i-Sharif with heavy losses last month by opposition forces. AIP identified the local commanders in Kunduz as Arif Khan of Jamiat-i-Islami, Arbab Mohammad Hashem of Hizb-i-Islami and Arbab Mohammad Ghulam of Ittehad-i-Islami.
